spec.rhs_for_integrator: Piecewise((0, Abs(F) <= (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0))*m*g), ((F - mu_k*m*g*sign(F)/(1 + beta*(1 - exp(-gamma*(1 + delta*log(1 + m*g/N0))*(Abs(F)/(m*g) - (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0)))))))/m, True))
sanity_expectations: For any fixed m and g, a is exactly 0 throughout the central sticking region |F| <= (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0))*m*g.

The width of the zero-acceleration region increases with normal load m*g because eta>0, so at the same normalized force ratio near mu_s a heavier or higher-g case can remain stuck while a lighter or lower-g case slides.
For fixed m and g in the sliding regime, a has the same sign as F and is approximately antisymmetric: a(-F,m,g) = -a(F,m,g).

For fixed m and g above breakaway, a(F,m,g) is not exactly affine in F; its incremental growth with |F| changes across the sliding branch because the opposing friction term weakens saturatingly rather than remaining constant.

At matched excess ratio above breakaway, changing load ratio m*g/N0 changes the mid-range sliding curvature because delta=0.5 modulates the effective exponential rate; the difference is strongest at moderate suprathreshold loads and weakens in the stuck limit and deep saturation limit.
Increasing g at fixed F and m can switch a trial from sliding to sticking near threshold, and when both trials slide, larger g generally reduces |a| by increasing frictional resistance.

spec.rationale: analyze_expression shows no derivatives/integrals and an explicit Piecewise algebraic mapping, so this is a static explicit relation for a(F,m,g) with remaining symbols fixed as parameters. Because freedom_change is none and g was explicitly declared as a varied V input in this record, preserve F, m, and g as sampled axes. Parameter choices are physically admissible and avoid the parent-recovery limits: eta>0 makes the static threshold depend measurably on normal load m*g; delta=0.5 with the provided constraint delta>-1 makes the suprathreshold exponential rate increase with load through 1+delta*log(1+m*g/N0), remaining positive over the chosen g,m ranges; beta=2 and gamma=3 give visible but not instant saturation of the sliding-friction weakening. The chosen ranges expose the recorded mechanisms. With m in 0.5-5 kg and g in 3-20 m/s^2, normal load m*g spans 1.5-100 N, so log(1+m*g/N0) varies substantially and both the load-dependent breakaway threshold and the load-dependent sliding-branch curvature are active. F in -30 to 30 N crosses zero and sweeps from subthreshold sticking into moderate and strong sliding for light and heavy loads without putting essentially all cases deep into saturation. Near threshold, different (m,g) at similar force ratio |F|/(m*g) can fall on different sides of stick-slip onset because of the eta*log(1+m*g/N0) term. Above threshold, the same excess ratio at different loads gives different acceleration curvature because delta couples load ratio into the effective weakening rate. Some high-load combinations within the F range will remain stuck over a broader central force window; that is intended because the branch transition itself is diagnostically important. No observation noise is added.

spec.scenario_text: A block rests on a horizontal rough surface while a signed horizontal force is applied. The response is its instantaneous horizontal acceleration, with the block remaining stationary below a fixed breakaway threshold and sliding friction opposing motion after that threshold is exceeded. Mass and applied force are independently varied while gravity and the two friction coefficients remain fixed.

response_change.parent_relation: Above the breakaway threshold, the parent gives a linear map from applied force to acceleration with constant slope 1/m and a constant offset from kinetic friction.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same stick-slip structure, but replace constant kinetic friction magnitude by a speed-weakening/applied-load-dependent effective sliding resistance so the post-breakaway acceleration is no longer exactly affine in F; its slope with respect to F changes across sliding conditions.
response_change.observable_effect: For fixed m and increasing |F| above breakaway, acceleration grows faster than the parent's straight-line prediction because the opposing sliding friction does not remain a constant magnitude over the whole sliding regime.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when |F| exceeds mu_s*m*g by a non-negligible margin so the block is in sliding, and across a range of suprathreshold loads large enough that assuming one constant kinetic-friction level becomes inaccurate.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate suprathreshold loads can already show slight non-affine post-breakaway acceleration versus F at fixed m; in holdout, the same curvature becomes clearer at larger static_margin without changing the sticking regime below threshold.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the effective sliding-friction law to a constant value mu_k independent of sliding condition, restoring a linear post-breakaway branch.
plan.gap_statement: The model idealizes kinetic friction as having a constant magnitude once sliding begins, giving one shared post-breakaway slope and offset for all suprathreshold forcing levels.
plan.baseline_assumption: Static and sliding friction coefficients are constant.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Real dry sliding contacts often show non-Coulomb kinetic friction, with effective sliding resistance varying across the sliding regime rather than remaining exactly constant after breakaway.
plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: for each fixed mass, acceleration is exactly zero for |F|<=mu_s*m*g, then becomes an affine antisymmetric function of F with slope 1/m and constant friction offset mu_k*g beyond threshold. A realistic next refinement is to relax only the constant-sliding-friction assumption while preserving zero acceleration in sticking and friction opposing motion. Varied conditions: sweep signed applied force F over subthreshold and suprathreshold values while holding g, mu_s, and the refined friction-law parameters fixed, and compare several masses m. Concrete contrast: at fixed m, the parent predicts that equal increments in F produce equal increments in a everywhere in the sliding regime; the child predicts changing incremental gain with |F| once sliding is active because the effective opposing friction is not constant. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary trajectory change, since a(F,m) itself changes on the observed static relation. Admissible activation is the sliding regime with sufficiently broad suprathreshold forcing; below threshold both parent and child still give a=0, so no contrast is claimed there. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce systematic curvature of a versus F across those sliding conditions because its post-breakaway branch is constrained to be exactly linear for each m.

response_change.observable_effect: At fixed m, just above breakaway the child can match the parent, but at larger |F|/(m*g) it can either level off or continue weakening more slowly/rapidly, changing the acceleration-versus-force bend without moving the zero-acceleration sticking branch.

response_change.parent_relation: The stick-slip boundary is a single Coulomb threshold |F|=mu_s*m*g, after which acceleration depends only on the suprathreshold force ratio through one shared breakaway level and a saturating sliding-friction weakening law.

contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying m and g already changes normal load and reveals near-threshold stick/slip differences; in holdout, the same load dependence extends to unseen normal-load levels without changing the antisymmetric force response.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the load-dependence amplitude to zero, so mu_s_eff becomes the constant mu_s and the threshold reverts to |F|=mu_s*m*g.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Real dry contacts can exhibit normal-load-dependent static adhesion/interlocking, making the effective breakaway coefficient vary with normal load even on a rigid horizontal surface.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the target mapping now depends jointly on the normalized tangential load and the separate normal load through a curved threshold surface, not a single shared threshold that can be shifted by refitting one constant.
contract.assumption_before: Static and sliding friction coefficients are constant.
contract.assumption_after: The effective static friction coefficient increases with normal load, so breakaway depends on m*g as well as force ratio.
contract.before_fragment: Piecewise((0, Abs(F) <= mu_s*m*g), ((F - mu_k*m*g*sign(F)/(1 + beta*(1 - exp(-gamma*(Abs(F)/(m*g) - mu_s)))))/m, True))
contract.after_fragment: Piecewise((0, Abs(F) <= (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0))*m*g), ((F - mu_k*m*g*sign(F)/(1 + beta*(1 - exp(-gamma*(Abs(F)/(m*g) - (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0)))))))/m, True))

contract.observable_signature: Parent response relationship: acceleration is exactly zero whenever |F|<=mu_s*m*g, and once sliding begins the acceleration is set by a suprathreshold weakening law tied to that same fixed breakaway coefficient. Child change: the onset threshold becomes (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0))*m*g, so both the branch switch and near-onset curvature in acceleration depend on normal load m*g in addition to force ratio. contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of all parent parameters cannot reproduce this contrast because any constant mu_s preserves one common normalized breakaway threshold Abs(F)/(m*g)=mu_s for every normal load. response_change.parent_relation: Above the load-dependent static threshold, the parent uses a single saturating weakening law for kinetic friction that depends only on the excess force ratio Abs(F)/(m*g) minus the breakaway level, so the acceleration-force curve has one fixed post-breakaway curvature shape for all admissible loads.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same stick-slip structure and antisymmetry, but relax the assumption that the suprathreshold weakening has one fixed saturation shape: let the effective kinetic resistance vary with normalized load m*g/N0 as well as excess force, so the post-breakaway acceleration curve changes curvature across masses or gravities even after accounting for the parent's existing static-threshold shift.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed normalized force ratio just above and moderately above breakaway, light-load and heavy-load cases show different rates of approach from breakaway friction toward asymptotic sliding friction; one shared parent parameter set cannot match both the near-threshold and farther-above-threshold acceleration curvature across those load conditions.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when Abs(F) exceeds the static threshold by an O(1/gamma) normalized excess and the explored load ratio m*g/N0 varies enough that contact-pressure effects can modify the weakening transition without violating dry-contact assumptions; the contrast is strongest for moderate suprathreshold forcing, not deep in the asymptotic large-force limit or fully stuck regime.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying F at several m or g values already reveals post-breakaway shape differences; in holdout, broader load ratios extend the same mechanism by changing how quickly the sliding friction approaches its asymptote after breakaway.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the new load-dependence of the suprathreshold weakening shape to zero, so the weakening law depends only on excess force as in the current equation.
plan.gap_statement: The current law allows normal load to shift the static breakaway threshold, but it still assumes a single universal post-breakaway weakening curve for kinetic friction across all normal loads.
plan.baseline_assumption: The mathematical form of suprathreshold kinetic-friction weakening is independent of normal load once force is measured relative to m*g and breakaway.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Real dry contacts can have pressure-dependent evolution of the sliding contact population, causing the Stribeck-like weakening transition width or saturation rate to depend on normal load even when the asymptotic Coulomb scale remains proportional to m*g.
plan.rationale: The parent target mapping is piecewise: zero acceleration below a load-dependent breakaway threshold, then an antisymmetric sliding branch whose friction drop from breakaway to kinetic saturation has one fixed shape set by beta and gamma. The effect is observable only in the sliding regime and before the weakening has fully saturated; in the stuck branch or at very large forcing the parent and child can look similar. No new input is needed because m and g already vary independently and supply the normal-load information required to expose the omitted interaction.

baseline_mechanisms: Static friction up to a finite limiting magnitude.
Constant-magnitude sliding friction opposing the applied motion.
baseline_assumptions: The surface is level and rigid.
The block is treated as a point mass for translational motion.
Static and sliding friction coefficients are constant.
scientific_constraints: Acceleration is zero in the sticking regime.
Sliding friction cannot assist the direction of impending or actual motion.

response_change.parent_relation: Above the breakaway threshold, the parent gives a linear map from applied force to acceleration with constant slope 1/m and a constant offset from kinetic friction.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same stick-slip structure, but replace constant kinetic friction magnitude by a speed-weakening/applied-load-dependent effective sliding resistance so the post-breakaway acceleration is no longer exactly affine in F; its slope with respect to F changes across sliding conditions.
response_change.observable_effect: For fixed m and increasing |F| above breakaway, acceleration grows faster than the parent's straight-line prediction because the opposing sliding friction does not remain a constant magnitude over the whole sliding regime.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when |F| exceeds mu_s*m*g by a non-negligible margin so the block is in sliding, and across a range of suprathreshold loads large enough that assuming one constant kinetic-friction level becomes inaccurate.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate suprathreshold loads can already show slight non-affine post-breakaway acceleration versus F at fixed m; in holdout, the same curvature becomes clearer at larger static_margin without changing the sticking regime below threshold.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the effective sliding-friction law to a constant value mu_k independent of sliding condition, restoring a linear post-breakaway branch.
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Real dry sliding contacts often show non-Coulomb kinetic friction, with effective sliding resistance varying across the sliding regime rather than remaining exactly constant after breakaway.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the sliding branch now depends on the joint normalized loading Abs(F)/(m*g), so the friction reduction and resulting acceleration curvature vary across both force and mass rather than through one shared constant offset.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Kinetic friction has constant magnitude mu_k*m*g throughout the sliding regime.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Kinetic friction weakens with suprathreshold normalized load after breakaway while still opposing motion.
evolution_contracts.after_fragment: Piecewise((0, Abs(F) <= mu_s*m*g), ((F - mu_k*m*g*sign(F)/(1 + beta*(Abs(F)/(m*g) - mu_s)))/m, True))
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: Parent response relationship: zero acceleration below breakaway and an exactly affine antisymmetric sliding branch in F for each fixed m. Child change: the post-breakaway branch bends upward in magnitude because the effective opposing friction decreases as the normalized load margin Abs(F)/(m*g) - mu_s grows. This changed target mapping is observable by sweeping F across subthreshold and suprathreshold values at fixed g, mu_s, mu_k, beta and comparing several masses m; below threshold both models coincide, while above threshold the child shows increasing incremental gain with |F| that the parent does not.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because once sliding is active its branch is constrained to (F - mu_k*m*g*sign(F))/m, which is exactly linear in F for each fixed m with constant slope 1/m and constant offset magnitude mu_k*g. Refitting mu_k, mu_s, or g can shift threshold or offset, but cannot create systematic curvature of a versus F across suprathreshold loads and masses simultaneously.

response_change.parent_relation: Above the static threshold |F|>mu_s*m*g, the parent gives an odd, monotone acceleration law whose suprathreshold friction weakening is controlled by one constant beta, so the post-breakaway curve versus normalized load |F|/(m*g) has one fixed shape for all masses and forces.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same stick/slip structure and antisymmetry, but relax the assumption that the weakening scale is globally constant by allowing the effective kinetic-friction decay with suprathreshold load to saturate nonlinearly, producing a different post-breakaway curvature as normalized load increases.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed m, just above breakaway the child can match the parent, but at larger |F|/(m*g) it can either level off or continue weakening more slowly/rapidly, changing the acceleration-versus-force bend without moving the zero-acceleration sticking branch.

evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: load-dependent saturation rate of suprathreshold friction weakening
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Real dry contacts can have pressure-dependent evolution of the sliding contact population, causing the Stribeck-like weakening transition width or saturation rate to depend on normal load even when the asymptotic Coulomb scale remains proportional to m*g.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the new parameter changes the effective relaxation scale inside the exponential transition through an interaction with load_ratio, so the post-breakaway curvature as a function of excess force is no longer universal across loads.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: A single load-independent suprathreshold weakening timescale gamma governs all admissible normal loads.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The suprathreshold weakening timescale is pressure-sensitive, with effective rate gamma*(1 + delta*log(1 + m*g/N0)).
evolution_contracts.before_fragment: Piecewise((0, Abs(F) <= (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0))*m*g), ((F - mu_k*m*g*sign(F)/(1 + beta*(1 - exp(-gamma*(Abs(F)/(m*g) - (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0)))))))/m, True))
evolution_contracts.after_fragment: Piecewise((0, Abs(F) <= (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0))*m*g), ((F - mu_k*m*g*sign(F)/(1 + beta*(1 - exp(-gamma*(1 + delta*log(1 + m*g/N0))*(Abs(F)/(m*g) - (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0)))))))/m, True))
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: The parent response is zero below the load-dependent threshold and otherwise follows one universal normalized post-breakaway curvature across all loads. The child keeps the same threshold branch but makes the sliding-branch curvature depend on load_ratio = m*g/N0 through the effective exponential rate, so for two different loads with matched excess_ratio the acceleration increments above breakaway differ most at moderate excess and converge again in the stuck and deep-saturation limits.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all existing parent parameters cannot absorb this across varying load_ratio because the parent has only one shared gamma and therefore one shared normalized transition width for every mass or gravity. Adjusting eta or N0 only shifts the threshold surface, while beta only changes the weakening amplitude, so a single parent parameter set cannot simultaneously fit different near-threshold-versus-midrange curvature patterns at low and high load.
